messages:
omar: Quick heads-up — after the slab->slotpager allocator change I saw a ~15% tail-latency bump for seq_len=2048 runs with flashv2. Repro steps and mini trace below. @mei @sasha

mei: Thanks, can you paste the bench command? :eyes:

omar: ./run/bench_attn --model=gpt-j-6b --seq=2048 --batch=1 --variant=flashv2 --kv-pager=slotpager --alloc=slot

sasha: got it. Which metric bumped? p99 or p999?

omar: p95 up ~8%, p99 up ~15%, p999 seen as sporadic spikes. CPU profiles show scheduler stalls during kv page reclamation.

ryan: any change in kernel selection? maybe flashv2 picks different kernel under slotpager.

omar: yes — runtime now prefers fused-path for short prefixes; but for paged paths kernel_router flips to FLASH_FUSED when kv_residency < 0.6. suspect back-and-forth thrash between fused and paged kernels.

mei: can you attach the perf flame? also logs showing 'kvpager: evict start' lines.

omar: pasted below:

--- perf flame snippet ---
40% nvptx_kernel_dispatch
20% kvpager::reclaim_pages
15% batcher::coalesce_wait
10% kernel_router::choose_kernel
---

kvpager log excerpt:
[info] kvpager: evict start shard=3 target=8 pages
[debug] kvpager: async writeback 2 pages
[warn] kvpager: backpressure apply -> throttle batching

sasha: 'backpressure apply' sounds new. Who added that throttle flag?

ryan: that was my change to avoid OOM when slabs fragment. It toggles batcher.hold = true while reclaiming.

sasha: hmm hold=true will block the dynamic_batcher until reclaim finishes — could lengthen latency a lot.

mei: suggestion: instead of full hold, set batcher.min_batch_size=1 and let partial batches pass. Also try lowering reclaim aggressiveness.

omar: tried lowering reclaim aggressiveness (reclaim_rate=0.5) — p99 improved ~6% but p95 still +4% compared to master.

bench-bot: quick benchmark: 10 iters seq=2048 batch=1 variant=flashv2 slotpager reclaim_rate=0.5 -> p95=112ms p99=210ms

ryan: can we flip kernel routing heuristic to prefer FLASH_PAGED when kv_residency < 0.8? Might avoid fused thrash for paged workloads.

omar: quick try: export KERNEL_ROUTER_MODE=paged_prefer and rerun.

sasha: also try enabling prefix-KV caching — many requests share first 512 tokens; that reduces reclaim pressure.

omar: added prefix cache, hitrate jumped to 0.24 -> p99 back to near-baseline on one run. promising but needs more runs.

mei: action items: 1) lower default reclaim aggressiveness for slotpager, 2) change batcher throttle to soft backoff (min_batch_size=1 + exponential cooloff), 3) add metric kvpager.eviction.throttle_count and expose in console.

sasha: I'll open a PR for batcher soft-backoff. ryan can modify kernel routing config. omar can add test harness and perf job.

omar: created a tiny repro env snippet:

export FLASH_VARIANT=flashv2
export KV_PAGER=slotpager
export SLOT_RECLAIM_RATE=0.5
export KERNEL_ROUTER_MODE=paged_prefer
./run/bench_attn --iters=50 --seq=2048 --batch=1

ryan: thanks — I'll run perf with kernel swap tracing enabled and post the differences.

devops-bot: deploybot: canary deploy option 'slotpager-softbackoff' scheduled for 03:00 UTC (pipeline #4921)

omar: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open for bench logs and traces.

bench-bot: follow-up run after soft-backoff patch: 25 iters seq=2048 batch=1 -> p95=98ms p99=145ms (roughly baseline)

mei: great. I'll add a perf alert: kvpager.eviction.throttle_count > 10/min triggers pager-eviction-oncall.

omar: :thumbsup:
